patronymicFormation.rule: For names ending in a hard consonant: add -ович (son) / -овна (daughter). For names ending in -й or soft consonant: add -евич / -евна. For names ending in -а/-я: drop ending, add -ич/-ична. The patronymic is used in formal address together with the first name (Иван Иванович), never with the surname alone.

relationships.dialectNote: Standard Russian (Москва/literary): отец (formal), папа (colloquial, post-18th c. from French papa), батя (informal/regional). Northern Archangel dialect: батя dominates colloquially; formal written form отец is universal across all regions. Southern Rostov dialect: тятя is an archaic but still-heard colloquial form. Siberian/Ural dialects: батяня and тятя appear. Pomor dialect: батя strongly dominant. Old Russian/Church Slavonic: отьць (Old East Slavic), отецъ (Church Slavonic), батюшка (affectionate/priestly address).

relationships.notes: Father. отец is the universal formal literary term across all dialects (Church Slavonic origin). папа is dominant informal Northern/urban colloquial form (from French papa, 18th c.). батя is widespread informally in Northern, Siberian, Ural, and Pomor dialects. тятя is characteristic of Southern (Rostov) and some Central dialects — archaic but still heard. metadata.dataSource: Ожегов и Шведова (1994) Толковый словарь русского языка; Vasmer (1950) Russisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch; Zaliznyak (1977) Grammaticheskiy slovar russkogo yazyka; Unbegaun (1969) Russian Grammar; Primary Chronicle for Old Russian forms; Dal (1863) Толковый словарь живого великорусского языка
metadata.kinshipSystem: Russian Lineal-Bifurcate with Speaker-Gender-Dependent In-Law Terms and Highly Asymmetric Affinal Network (6-case inflection, patronymic system, distinct test'/svyokor in-law sets)
metadata.specialNote: Russian kinship is unique for: (1) Full 6-case noun declension — every kinship term has 6 forms; (2) Patronymic (отчество) system — every person carries a middle name from their father; (3) Highly asymmetric in-law system — husband and wife have COMPLETELY DIFFERENT terms for the same in-law; (4) Old Russian preserved DISTINCT paternal/maternal uncle terms (стрый vs уй) now lost; (5) Speaker gender determines many in-law terms.
